html:
A relaxed, quiet style of samba that grew up in the late 1950s among young musicians in the beach neighbourhoods of Rio de Janeiro. The name means roughly "new trend".

Its start is often dated to 1958, when the singer and guitarist João Gilberto recorded "Chega de Saudade", written by Antônio Carlos Jobim with words by the poet Vinicius de Moraes. Gilberto's guitar boiled the samba rhythm down to a soft, syncopated pulse, and he sang almost in a whisper. Jobim added rich harmonies influenced by jazz and classical music.

It became a symbol of a confident, modern Brazil in the years of the new capital, Brasília. In 1962 a concert at Carnegie Hall and the album Jazz Samba spread it in the United States. "The Girl from Ipanema", recorded by Gilberto and Stan Getz with Astrud Gilberto singing, became a world hit in 1964. That same year Brazil's military coup came, and many musicians turned to more political songs.
sum: A relaxed, quiet style of samba that grew up in the late 1950s among young musicians in the beach neighbourhoods of Rio de Janeiro. The name means roughly "new trend".
